title: Drain the Issue Queue
bottom_line: It works through every open GitHub issue labeled `ai` one by one, merging a PR for each, until none remain, then sends a push notification.

sections.heading: It commits, pushes and merges on its own, so agree first

cards.title: Fully automatic by design
cards.text: It auto-commits, auto-pushes and auto-merges without asking at each step. That is its entire purpose.

cards.title: Confirm before the first run
cards.text: Claude confirms with you before the first run that this is what you want for this repository and branch.

sections.heading: Set up the GitHub CLI and ntfy before you start

cards.title: git and GitHub CLI
cards.text: Install `git` and `gh`, signed in with `gh auth login`, with push access to the repository. Every issue, PR and status command goes through `gh`.

cards.title: ntfy server set
cards.text: The `ntfy` plugin installs with plan-tools; its `ntfy:ntfy` skill sends the push notifications. Set its `server` setting first; see the ntfy README.

cards.title: Issues to work on
cards.text: Open GitHub issues labeled `ai` (or your `--label` name). `/plan-tools:write-issue` creates these.

blocks.text: Installing plan-tools installs `ntfy` together with its other dependencies, `fastapi-template` and `htmx-vs-alpine`.

sections.heading: Run it bare, or pick a model and a label

blocks.code: /plan-tools:drain-issues [optional model override, e.g. "opus" — defaults to sonnet] [--label <name>]
blocks.caption: Both parts are optional.

blocks.title: What you can pass
rows: The model each cycle's helper runs on. One of `sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`.
Works through issues with `<name>` instead of `ai`, uses it in the notifications, and passes it on to `impl-issue`, `finalize-pr` and `write-issue` in every cycle.

blocks.title: Example: issues labeled backlog, on opus
Defaults shared across the plugin
rows: Deferred work goes into GitHub issues labeled `ai`
A model word in the arguments, for example `opus`

blocks.text: Before the loop starts, it works out the repository's main branch once. If that is unclear, it asks you.

sections.heading: Each issue goes through one full cycle, then the loop repeats

steps.title: Checks for work
steps.text: It looks for an open issue with the label. If there is none, it sends "No issues left — no open ai-labeled issues" with title "drain-issues" and priority 4, and stops.

steps.title: Implements the oldest issue
steps.text: A fresh helper, on the chosen model and with a clean context, runs in the background. It follows `impl-issue`: a branch off the main branch, the fix, and a commit with a `Closes #<number>` line.

steps.title: Reviews and tests
steps.text: It follows `finalize-pr` on the change: code review with fixes (`code-review --fix`), a test plan written and run, and leftover items recorded as new issues with `write-issue`.

steps.title: Opens the PR
steps.text: It pushes the branch and opens a PR with the `Closes #<number>` line, so the issue closes on merge. New follow-up issues are listed under a "Follow-ups" section.

steps.title: Waits for checks, then merges
steps.text: It checks the PR's checks every 5 minutes. When all pass, it merges. When any fail, it fixes the break, commits, pushes and keeps waiting.

steps.title: Resets and goes again
steps.text: After a merge, it checks out the main branch, fetches, and resets it hard to `origin/<main branch>`. Then it goes back to the first step.

blocks.title: Each cycle reports back
items: The final status: merged, stopped for a decision, or stuck.

sections.heading: You get a push notification whenever the loop stops

blocks.text: What happens next depends on the final report of each cycle's helper.

cards.title: Needs your decision
cards.text: On something hard, significant, or a decision only you can make, the helper sends a notification describing the blocker and stops rather than guessing. The loop waits for you.

cards.title: Stuck
cards.text: On an unresolved failure, it sends a notification describing what is stuck and stops the loop.

cards.title: Helper died mid-run
cards.text: Every 20 minutes it checks the helper is alive. If it is gone without a completion report, it sends a notification that the cycle died mid-run and stops the loop.

cards.title: Queue empty
cards.text: When no open labeled issues remain, it sends "No issues left" and stops.

blocks.text: The 20-minute check is only a safety net for a helper that died silently. It does not replace the normal completion report.

next_action.text: Set the ntfy plugin's `server` setting, then run `/plan-tools:drain-issues` and confirm when asked.
next_action.detail: The plugin README says to set the ntfy `server` setting first; see the ntfy README.
